facts.text: EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 is a law dated 5 August 2022 that entered into force on 15 September 2022; the cited consolidated version is dated 24 March 2026.
facts.quote: (5 August 2022, in force 15 September 2022, consolidated version 24 March 2026; law)

facts.text: EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 covers type approval of automated driving systems in fully automated vehicles.
facts.quote: It covers the type approval of automated driving systems in fully automated vehicles.

facts.text: Annex III Part 4 of EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 sets principles for credibility assessment for using a virtual toolchain in ADS validation.
facts.quote: Annex III Part 4 sets the "principles for credibility assessment for using virtual toolchain in ADS validation".

facts.text: EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 requires documentation of each model's validation method and acceptance thresholds, validation data and scenarios that sufficiently reflect the ODD, a criticality assessment, and characterization of variability in results.
facts.quote: It requires documentation of each model's validation method and acceptance thresholds; validation data and scenarios that "sufficiently reflect the ODD"; a criticality assessment; a characterization of the variability of results;

facts.text: EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 requires the outcome of the current credibility assessment to define the envelope in which the virtual tool can be used.
facts.quote: "the outcome of the current credibility assessment shall define the envelope in which the virtual tool can be used"

facts.text: UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM) is a guideline identified as ECE/TRANS/WP.29/2022/58, with updated master document WP.29-189-07 dated March 2023.
facts.quote: **UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM)** (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/2022/58; updated master document WP.29-189-07, March 2023; guideline).

entities.name: UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM)

facts.text: UNECE NATM has five pillars: audit and assessment, virtual testing, track testing, real-world testing, and in-service monitoring.
facts.quote: It has five pillars: audit and assessment, virtual testing, track testing, real-world testing and in-service monitoring.

entities.name: UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM)

facts.text: UNECE NATM's credibility framework covers toolchain description, scope, modeling assumptions and limits, criticality, verification, validation, and management, people and data quality.
facts.quote: Its credibility framework covers description of the toolchain; scope; modeling assumptions and limits; criticality; verification; validation; and management, people and data quality.

entities.name: UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM)

facts.text: Under UNECE NATM, virtual testing is one part of a wider assessment, not a simulation-only approval regime.
facts.quote: Virtual testing is one part of a wider assessment, not a simulation-only approval regime

entities.name: UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM)

facts.text: UNECE NATM requires virtual-toolchain credibility to be demonstrated for the toolchain's intended scope.
facts.quote: virtual-toolchain credibility has to be demonstrated for its intended scope.

entities.name: UNECE New Assessment/Test Method for Automated Driving (NATM)

facts.text: UN Regulation No. 171 on Driver Control Assistance Systems, with regulatory text published in 2024–2025, incorporates credibility-assessment principles when a virtual toolchain is used.
facts.quote: **UN Regulation No. 171 (Driver Control Assistance Systems; regulatory text published 2024 to 2025)** incorporates principles for credibility assessment when a virtual toolchain is used.

facts.text: Supplements to UN Regulation No. 152 for car and van AEBS adopted by WP.29 in 2025 permit virtual testing as an alternative to some physical tests.
facts.quote: **UN Regulation No. 152 (car and van AEBS).** Supplements adopted by WP.29 in 2025 permit virtual testing as an alternative to some physical tests.

facts.text: The UN R152 proposal text has two pillars: validating the virtual method by comparison with physical results, then using virtual results for approval.
facts.quote: The proposal text has two "pillars": validation of the virtual method by comparison with physical results, then use of virtual results for approval.

facts.text: WP.29 text ECE/TRANS/WP.29/2025/141 dated 28 August 2025 states that confirmatory validation for UN R152 virtual testing shall include physical tests, with the number agreed between manufacturer and authority.
facts.quote: The WP.29 text of 28 August 2025 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/2025/141) states that confirmatory validation "shall include physical tests", in a number "defined in agreement between" manufacturer and authority.

facts.text: A February 2025 vendor commentary on UN R152 virtual testing reports that at least 30% of required tests must remain physical, including at least one test for each scenario variant relevant to approval.
facts.quote: A vendor commentary (February 2025) reports that "at least 30% of the required tests must still be conducted physically, with at least one test for each scenario variant relevant to approval"

facts.text: The France/UTAC CERAM working document AEBS-16-03 includes a 30% physical-test figure alongside virtual validation with 11 variables (SUT+Target) and three metrics: IAPE, Double th, and interval.
facts.quote: France/UTAC CERAM working document AEBS-16-03 ("Virtual validation 11 variables (SUT+Target), 3 Metrics: IAPE, Double th, interval + 30% Physical tests")

facts.text: The reported 30% physical-test figure for UN R152 should not be treated as settled for the adopted text.
facts.quote: The 30% figure should not be treated as settled for the adopted text

facts.text: The reported UN R152 30% physical-test figure should not be transferred to off-road machines without justification.
facts.quote: should not be transferred to off-road machines without justification.

facts.text: In January 2024, the United Kingdom submitted regulator-level expert document GRVA-18-55 arguing that the R152 proposal did not address all aspects of a credible virtual testing capability.
facts.quote: in January 2024 the United Kingdom submitted expert document GRVA-18-55 arguing that the R152 proposal "does not address all the aspects of a credible virtual testing capability"

facts.text: The United Kingdom's January 2024 regulator-level expert document GRVA-18-55 argued that the R152 proposal appeared to require physical testing only for the final toolchain, whereas physical testing should be used and evidenced for every toolchain component.
facts.quote: "Physical Testing appears only to be required for the final toolchain... Physical Testing should be used and evidenced for all the components of the toolchain"

facts.text: In November 2025, the Russian Federation proposed mandatory physical testing to verify the virtual model in the UN R152 discussion; the passage identifies this as a regulator-level expert position.
facts.quote: In November 2025 the Russian Federation proposed mandatory physical testing to verify the virtual model. Both are regulator-level expert positions.

facts.text: ISO 34502:2022, ISO 34503:2023, ISO 34504:2024 and ISO 34505:2025 provide vocabulary and methods for ADS scenario-based safety evaluation, operational design domain specification, scenario categorization and test-case generation.
facts.quote: **ISO 34502:2022, ISO 34503:2023, ISO 34504:2024 and ISO 34505:2025** provide vocabulary and methods for scenario-based safety evaluation of automated driving systems, operational design domain specification, scenario categorization and test-case generation.

facts.text: ISO 34502:2022, ISO 34503:2023, ISO 34504:2024 and ISO 34505:2025 address the coverage problem more than the model-credibility problem.
facts.quote: They solve the coverage problem more than the model-credibility problem

facts.text: ISO 34502:2022, ISO 34503:2023, ISO 34504:2024 and ISO 34505:2025 establish no physical-to-virtual test ratio.
facts.quote: establish no physical-to-virtual ratio.

facts.text: ISO/PAS 34506 is intended for qualification of virtual test environments, but remained under development in October 2026 and should not be treated as a finished standard.
facts.quote: ISO/PAS 34506, intended for qualification of virtual test environments, was still under development in October 2026 and should not be treated as a finished standard.

facts.text: ISO 34502, ISO 34503, ISO 34504, ISO 34505 and draft ISO/PAS 34506 do not demonstrate validity for mines, quarries, earthworks, deformable surfaces, machine articulation, dense dust, unusual object geometries, or heavy mobile machinery vibration and contamination conditions.
facts.quote: None of these demonstrates validity for mines, quarries, earthworks, deformable surfaces, machine articulation, dense dust, unusual object geometries or the vibration and contamination conditions of heavy mobile machinery.
